"""Anonymise harvested mail into committable fixtures.

Structure is preserved exactly — quote markers and their depth, sentinel lines,
where an attribution wraps, header-block shape, blank lines, CRLF. Only identities
and prose are replaced, because structure is what the extractor is tested on and
prose is what carries the confidential content.

Three bugs this version exists to avoid:

1. The `Name <addr>` pair regex must not cross a comma and must not contain
   digits, or `On Tue, 3 Feb 2026 at 07:36, Alice <a@x> wrote:` matches from "On"
   and the whole date is replaced as a display name.
2. It must also not cross a COLON, or `From: Jane <j@x>` matches from "From" and
   the header KEY is eaten — which silently destroyed 11 of the 20 header lines in
   the first `many-header-blocks` fixture.
3. `Subject:` is structural but its text is content: keep the key and its
   Re:/FW:/Fwd: prefix chain, replace the subject text like any prose.
"""
import json, re, hashlib, random, unicodedata

FIRST = ["Jean-Luc","William","Beverly","Geordi","Deanna","Tasha","Noonien","Bruce",
         "Leah","Orfil","Reginald","Miles","Alyssa","Ro","Katherine","Selar","Tam",
         "Nella","Kathryn","Chakotay","Tuvok","Harry","Neelix","Seven","Kes",
         "Benjamin","Kira","Jadzia","Julian","Odo","Quark","Jake","Ezri","Worf",
         "Christopher","Una","Spock","Nyota","Hikaru","Pavel","Leonard","Montgomery",
         "Michael","Saru","Sylvia","Paul","Hugh","Cleveland","Jett","Zora"]
LAST  = ["Picard","Riker","Crusher","Forge","Troi","Yar","Soong","Maddox","Brahms",
         "Quinteros","Barclay","OBrien","Ogawa","Laren","Pulaski","Vex","Elbrun",
         "Daren","Janeway","Torres","Kim","Paris","Tuvix","Sisko","Nerys","Dax",
         "Bashir","Ishka","Pike","Chin-Riley","Uhura","Sulu","Chekov","McCoy",
         "Scott","Burnham","Stamets","Culber","Booker","Rhys","Detmer","Owosekun"]
CAST = [f"{f} {l}" for f in FIRST for l in LAST]
DOMAINS = ["starfleet.fed","daystrom.fed","utopia-planitia.fed","vulcan.fed",
           "risa.fed","bajor.fed","cardassia.fed","ferenginar.fed","trill.fed",
           "andoria.fed","betazed.fed","qonos.fed","tellar.fed","earth.fed"]
FILLER = ("the telemetry export the berth registry the levy column the sensor "
          "readings the statement run the fellow number the settlement window "
          "the reconciliation the manifest the shipment record the audit trail").split()

people, domains, locals_ = {}, {}, {}
cast_used = set()
# Every token the cast can be made of. The single-token name pass must never
# rewrite a name it just invented, or "Jean-Luc Picard" becomes "Deanna Deanna".
CAST_TOKENS = {t for n in CAST for t in re.split(r'[\s\-]+', n)} | set(FIRST) | set(LAST)

def person(raw):
    key = raw.strip().lower()
    if key not in people:
        n = len(people)
        people[key] = CAST[n % len(CAST)] + ("" if n < len(CAST) else str(n))
        cast_used.add(people[key])
    return people[key]

def domain(raw):
    key = raw.lower()
    if key not in domains:
        n = len(domains)
        domains[key] = DOMAINS[n % len(DOMAINS)] + ("" if n < len(DOMAINS) else str(n) + ".fed")
    return domains[key]

def addr(raw):
    key = raw.strip().lower()
    if key not in locals_:
        name = person(key).lower().replace(" ", ".").replace("-", "")
        at = key.rsplit("@", 1)
        locals_[key] = f"{name}@{domain(at[1]) if len(at) > 1 else DOMAINS[0]}"
    return locals_[key]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- identity masks
reEmail   = re.compile(r'[A-Za-z0-9._%+\-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.\-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}')
reURL     = re.compile(r'(?:https?://|www\.)[^\s>\]\)]+')
rePhone   = re.compile(r'(?<!\d)(?:\+?\d[\d\s\-()]{7,}\d)(?!\d)')
reMoney   = re.compile(r'[$£€]\s?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?')
reLongNum = re.compile(r'\b\d{6,}\b')
# Bug 1 + bug 2: no comma, no semicolon, no digit, no COLON in the display-name
# lead. Also no asterisk, or Outlook's bold chrome in "*From:* Jane <j@x>" is
# swallowed into the display name and the flattened-bold key shape is lost.
rePair    = re.compile(r'([^<>@\n,;:*0-9]{2,45}?)\s*<\s*'
                       r'((?:mailto:)?[A-Za-z0-9._%+\-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.\-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,})\s*>')

def _pair(m):
    lead, target = m.group(1), m.group(2)
    keep = lead[: len(lead) - len(lead.lstrip())]          # preserve leading whitespace
    quoted = lead.strip().startswith('"') and lead.strip().endswith('"')
    bare = target[7:] if target.startswith("mailto:") else target
    nm = person(bare)
    if quoted:
        nm = f'"{nm}"'
    pre = "mailto:" if target.startswith("mailto:") else ""
    return f"{keep}{nm} <{pre}{addr(bare)}>"

def scrub_identities(s):
    s = rePair.sub(_pair, s)          # pairs first, so name and address agree
    s = reEmail.sub(lambda m: addr(m.group(0)), s)
    s = reURL.sub("https://example.fed/x", s)
    s = rePhone.sub("+61 4 0000 0000", s)
    s = reMoney.sub("$0.00", s)
    s = reLongNum.sub(lambda m: "9" * len(m.group(0)), s)
    return s

# Words that must survive on a structural line, because the parser tests them:
# openers, header keys, rule words, and every weekday / month / meridiem /
# timezone token that can appear in a date we are deliberately keeping verbatim.
KEEP = set("""on le el il em am op den pa pe w dnia dniu vao from sent to subject cc bcc
date reply begin original forwarded message importance priority attachments
mon tue tues wed weds thu thur thurs fri sat sun monday tuesday wednesday thursday
friday saturday sunday jan feb mar apr may jun jul aug sep sept oct nov dec
january february march april june july august september october november december
pm gmt utc bst est edt cst cdt mst mdt pst pdt aest aedt acst acdt awst nzst nzdt
ist cet cest sgt hkt jst wib at wrote von gesendet an betreff de enviado para
asunto objet envoye van verzonden aan da inviato oggetto fra sendt skickat till
amne assunto re fw fwd aw sv tr t z""".split())

reWordRun   = re.compile(r"\b[A-Z][A-Za-z'\-]*(?:\s+[A-Z][A-Za-z'\-]*){1,3}\b")
reWordOne   = re.compile(r"\b[A-Z][A-Za-z'\-]{1,}\b")
reHasDigit  = re.compile(r'\d')

def _keepable(tok):
    return unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", tok).encode("ascii", "ignore").decode().lower().strip("'-") in KEEP

def scrub_names(s):
    """Map every human-looking name run, then every leftover capitalised token.

    The second pass is what stops a one-word company or a first-name-only
    attribution ("... , Jane wrote:") from surviving verbatim.
    """
    def run(m):
        t = m.group(0)
        if t in cast_used or reHasDigit.search(t):
            return t
        if all(w in CAST_TOKENS for w in re.split(r'[\s]+', t)):
            return t
        if all(_keepable(w) for w in t.split()):
            return t
        return person(t)
    s = reWordRun.sub(run, s)

    def one(m):
        t = m.group(0)
        if t in cast_used or _keepable(t) or reHasDigit.search(t):
            return t
        if t in CAST_TOKENS or all(w in CAST_TOKENS for w in t.split('-')):
            return t
        return person(t).split()[0]
    return reWordOne.sub(one, s)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- structure
# Group 1 is the whole key including Outlook's bold-flattening chrome, re-emitted
# verbatim so *From:* / *From: * / From: all survive as themselves — unbold() in
# the parser is tested against exactly those four dialects.
reHdrKey     = re.compile(r'(?i)^(\*?(from|sent|to|subject|cc|bcc|date|reply-to|'
                          r'von|gesendet|an|betreff|de|enviado|para|asunto|objet|envoyé|'
                          r'van|verzonden|aan|da|inviato|oggetto|fra|sendt|skickat|till|ämne|assunto)'
                          r'\*?[ \t]*:[ \t]*\*?[ \t]*)(.*)$')
IDENTITY_KEYS = {"from","to","cc","bcc","reply-to","von","an","de","para","van","aan","fra","till"}
reRule       = re.compile(r'^([-_*]{4,}|-{2,}\s?forwarded message\s?-{2,}|'
                          r'-{3,}\s?original message\s?-{3,}|begin forwarded message\s*:)', re.I)
reSig        = re.compile(r'^-- $')
reSubject    = re.compile(r'(?i)^(\*?(?:subject|betreff|asunto|objet|oggetto|ämne|assunto)\*?[ \t]*:'
                          r'[ \t]*\*?[ \t]*(?:(?:re|fw|fwd|aw|sv|tr)[ \t]*:[ \t]*)*)(.*)$')
reDepth      = re.compile(r'^([ \t]*(?:>[ \t]*)*)(.*)$')
reSep        = re.compile(r'(\r\n|\r|\n)')

OPENERS = ["on","le","el","il","em","am","op","den","på","pe","w dniu","dnia","vào","在"]
CLOSERS = ["wrote:","sent:","a écrit :","a écrit:","écrit:","escribió:","ha scritto:",
           "scritto:","escreveu:","schrieb:","schreef:","napisał:","napisała:","pisze:",
           "skrev:","kirjoitti:","đã viết:","写道：","작성:"]
MAXWRAP = 5

def starts_with_opener(t):
    l = t.strip().lower()
    return any(l == o or l.startswith(o + " ") or l.startswith(o + " ") for o in OPENERS)

def has_closer(t):
    l = t.lower()
    return any(c in l for c in CLOSERS)

def attribution_index(texts):
    """Indexes of every line that is part of an attribution.

    Mirrors sentinel.go FindAttribution's join, so an opener whose `wrote:` sits on
    a continuation line is recognised as structural and kept verbatim. Getting this
    wrong turns a wrapped attribution's first line into filler and destroys the
    exact case the corpus exists to cover.
    """
    marked = set()
    for i, t in enumerate(texts):
        if has_closer(t):
            marked.add(i)
        if not starts_with_opener(t):
            continue
        parts = []
        for j in range(i, min(len(texts), i + MAXWRAP + 1)):
            tj = texts[j].strip()
            if tj == "" and j > i:
                break
            if j > i and starts_with_opener(tj):
                break
            parts.append(tj)
            if has_closer(" ".join(parts)):
                marked.update(range(i, j + 1))
                break
    return marked

def filler_like(text, seed):
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    words = text.split()
    if not words:
        return text
    s = " ".join(rnd.choice(FILLER) for _ in words)
    if text.rstrip().endswith((".", ":", "?", "!")):
        s += text.rstrip()[-1]
    return s

def rewrite_header_value(key, value):
    """Rebuild an identity header's value from the cast, part by part.

    Preserves the recipient count, the separators and whether each part carried an
    angle-bracketed address — the shape a header-block parser reads — while
    guaranteeing no source name survives even when a part is a bare one-word
    company with no address at all.
    """
    if key.lower() not in IDENTITY_KEYS:
        return None
    out, buf = [], ""
    for part in re.split(r'(,|;)', value):
        if part in (",", ";"):
            out.append(part)
            continue
        lead = part[: len(part) - len(part.lstrip())]
        core = part.strip()
        if not core:
            out.append(part)
            continue
        em = reEmail.search(core)
        if em and "<" in core:
            out.append(f"{lead}{person(em.group(0))} <{addr(em.group(0))}>")
        elif em:
            out.append(f"{lead}{addr(em.group(0))}")
        elif core.lower() in ("undisclosed-recipients:;", "undisclosed recipients"):
            out.append(part)
        else:
            out.append(f"{lead}{person(core)}")
    return "".join(out)

def structural_line(text, attr_marked):
    stripped = text.strip()
    return bool(reHdrKey.match(stripped) or reRule.match(stripped)
                or reSig.match(text) or attr_marked)

def anonymise_line(raw_text, i, attr_marked):
    """One depth-stripped line. Returns the replacement text."""
    stripped = raw_text.strip()
    if structural_line(raw_text, attr_marked):
        t = scrub_identities(raw_text)
        mh = reHdrKey.match(t.strip())
        ms = reSubject.match(t.strip())
        if ms:
            # Subject: the key and its Re:/FW: chain are structural, the text is not.
            lead = t[: len(t) - len(t.lstrip())]
            return lead + ms.group(1) + filler_like(ms.group(2), f"subj{i}")
        if mh and mh.group(2).lower() in IDENTITY_KEYS:
            lead = t[: len(t) - len(t.lstrip())]
            rv = rewrite_header_value(mh.group(2), mh.group(3))
            if rv is not None:
                return lead + mh.group(1) + rv
        return apply_denylist(scrub_names(t))
    return scrub_identities(raw_text) if False else filler_like(
        scrub_identities(raw_text), f"{i}:{hashlib.sha1(raw_text.encode()).hexdigest()[:8]}")

def anonymise_body(body):
    """Rewrite a body in place, leaving every line separator exactly as it was.

    Separators are split out and re-emitted verbatim rather than normalised to
    CRLF: one message in this mailbox is CR CR LF throughout and 45 more mix bare
    LF into CRLF, and rewriting those would move the line boundaries the parser
    sees — and would change a census taken on the source.
    """
    parts = reSep.split(body)
    texts = parts[0::2]
    split = [reDepth.match(t).groups() for t in texts]
    attr_marked = attribution_index([t for _, t in split])
    out = []
    for i, (prefix, text) in enumerate(split):
        if text.strip() == "":
            out.append(prefix.rstrip() if prefix.strip() else "")
        else:
            out.append(prefix + anonymise_line(text, i, i in attr_marked))
    res = []
    for i, t in enumerate(out):
        res.append(t)
        if 2 * i + 1 < len(parts):
            res.append(parts[2 * i + 1])
    return "".join(res)


def anonymise_headerfield(key, value, seed=""):
    if not value:
        return value
    v = scrub_identities(value)
    if key.lower() in IDENTITY_KEYS:
        return rewrite_header_value(key, v)
    if key.lower() == "subject":
        m = re.match(r'(?i)^((?:(?:re|fw|fwd|aw|sv|tr)\s*:\s*)*)(.*)$', v)
        return m.group(1) + filler_like(m.group(2), "subj" + seed)
    return scrub_names(v)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- denylist pass
# A final safety net over structural lines, which are the only lines kept
# verbatim. Two leak classes got through everything above and were caught by the
# audit's probes:
#
#   1. an address split across a soft line break — "... jane.doe@" on one
#      line and "acmeco.com" on the next — matches no email pattern on either
#      line, so the local part survived intact;
#   2. a lowercase organisation inside a display name ("Jane Doe from acmeco"),
#      which neither the name-run nor the capitalised-token pass can see.
#
# So every token that appears anywhere in the source as an address label or as
# part of a name is denied outright and mapped to a cast-derived token.
reFragLocal  = re.compile(r'[A-Za-z0-9._%+\-]{2,}@')
reFragDomain = re.compile(r'@[A-Za-z0-9.\-]{2,}')
reBareDomain = re.compile(r'\b[A-Za-z][A-Za-z\-]{1,}(?:\.[A-Za-z][A-Za-z\-]{1,})+\b')
reToken      = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z'\-]{2,}")

deny = {}          # lowercased source token -> replacement token
SAFE = {t.lower() for t in CAST_TOKENS} | {"example", "fed", "mailto", "https", "http"}
SAFE |= {lab for d in DOMAINS for lab in d.split(".")}

def prune_cast(source_tokens):
    """Drop any invented name that collides with a real token from the source.

    Without this, a cast member called Michael makes the leak audit unfalsifiable
    for every real Michael in the mailbox: the probe cannot tell an invented name
    from a surviving one.
    """
    global CAST, CAST_TOKENS, FIRST, LAST
    low = {t.lower() for t in source_tokens}
    FIRST = [f for f in FIRST if not any(p.lower() in low for p in re.split(r'[\s\-]+', f))]
    LAST = [l for l in LAST if not any(p.lower() in low for p in re.split(r'[\s\-]+', l))]
    CAST = [f"{f} {l}" for f in FIRST for l in LAST]
    CAST_TOKENS = {t for n in CAST for t in re.split(r'[\s\-]+', n)} | set(FIRST) | set(LAST)
    if not CAST:
        raise SystemExit("every cast name collided with the source")


def source_tokens(texts):
    toks = set()
    for s in texts:
        for a in reEmail.findall(s):
            local, _, dom = a.partition("@")
            toks |= set(re.split(r'[._%+\-]+', local))
            toks |= set(dom.split("."))
        for r in reWordRun.findall(s):
            toks |= set(re.split(r"[\s\-']+", r))
        for m in reFragLocal.finditer(s):
            toks |= set(re.split(r'[._%+\-]+', m.group(0)[:-1]))
        for m in reBareDomain.finditer(s):
            toks |= set(m.group(0).split("."))
    return toks


def build_denylist(texts):
    """Collect every token the source uses as an address label or in a name, prune
    the cast of anything that collides with it, then map each denied token."""
    global SAFE
    toks = source_tokens(texts)
    prune_cast(toks)
    SAFE = {t.lower() for t in CAST_TOKENS} | {"example", "fed", "mailto", "https", "http"}
    SAFE |= {lab for d in DOMAINS for lab in d.split(".")}
    for t in sorted(toks):
        tl = t.lower()
        if len(tl) < 3 or tl in SAFE or _keepable(t) or tl in deny:
            continue
        deny[tl] = person("token:" + tl).split()[0]

def _match_case(src, repl):
    if src.isupper():
        return repl.upper()
    if src.islower():
        return repl.lower()
    return repl

def apply_denylist(s):
    def one(m):
        t = m.group(0)
        r = deny.get(t.lower())
        return _match_case(t, r) if r else t
    s = reToken.sub(one, s)
    # An address fragment left dangling by a soft line break keeps its shape —
    # "local@" stays "local@" and "@domain" stays "@domain" — so the wrap point
    # the parser sees does not move.
    s = reFragLocal.sub(lambda m: addr(m.group(0) + "x.fed").split("@")[0] + "@", s)
    s = reFragDomain.sub(lambda m: "@" + domain(m.group(0)[1:]), s)
    return s
